title: Event Boundaries as Temporal Cuts
content_html:
Event Boundaries as Temporal Cuts

Event segmentation research shows that perception discretizes continuous experience into events; these boundaries strongly shape encoding, retrieval, and prediction.

Event boundaries are cognitive “cuts” through continuous experience. They increase encoding at the boundary, restructure associations, and determine what is remembered or forgotten. Boundaries are the mind’s editing points.

  1. Segmentation: Observers spontaneously mark boundaries in films and narratives; brain activity shifts at those points (e.g., hippocampus, posterior medial network).
  2. Memory effects: Items across a boundary are less associated; within‑event items bind more strongly. Boundary moments are well remembered but can disrupt temporal order.
  3. Prediction: Boundaries trigger model updates; prediction errors increase around them, aiding learning of structure.
